candidate_evidence.quote: Participants undergoing resection for a presumed newly-diagnosed glioblastoma (WHO grade 4) will be treated with niraparib for 4 days prior to surgical resection.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: will enroll up to 24 participants with newly-diagnosed glioblastoma and up to 18 recurrent glioma participants with IDH mutation and ATRX loss.

combines therapeutic dosing of niraparib plus standard-of-care fractionated radiotherapy (in Arm A) or niraparib monotherapy (in Arm B) until progression of disease.

source_quote.quote: Participants undergoing resection of a recurrent WHO Grade II, III, or IV glioma with IDH1 or IDH2 mutation and ATRX loss will be treated with niraparib for 4 days prior to a planned surgical resection.

coder_notes: Early Phase 1 (Phase 0) trigger trial: translational subset. Arm A newly diagnosed GBM (niraparib + RT in expansion); Arm B recurrent IDH-mutant ATRX-loss grade II-IV glioma (niraparib monotherapy). regimen coded combination because Arm A includes radiotherapy; Arm B is monotherapy. cns5_terminology historical: 'Glioblastoma Multiforme' in conditions and 'WHO grade 4' GBM without IDH requirement; Arm B includes IDH-mutant grade IV glioma. control_arm_from_other_arms coded no (two experimental arms, neither a control). The IDH/ATRX enrichment match to niraparib is based on mechanistic plausibility only and is flagged for adjudication.
